[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 3 1. SHORT TITLE, APPLICABILITY AND DEFINITIONS 1.1 These regulations shall be called the [Institution Name] Academic Regulations 2026 and apply to all students admitted to undergraduate programmes from the academic year 2026-27 onwards. 1.2 The Academic Council is the competent authority to frame, amend and interpret these regulations, subject to approval of the Governing Body and the requirements of statutory bodies. 1.3 In these regulations, unless the context requires otherwise: (a) Academic Year means a period of two consecutive semesters (odd and even), each with a minimum of 90 working days. (b) Credit is a unit of measure of the weekly workload: one hour of lecture or tutorial, or two to three hours of practical work, per week per semester. (c) Course means a theory, practical, project, or any other component of the curriculum carrying a unique code. (d) CGPA and SGPA mean Cumulative and Semester Grade Point Average respectively. (e) Head of Department (HoD), Principal and Controller of Examinations (CoE) have their usual institutional meanings. 2. ADMISSION AND ELIGIBILITY 2.1 Admission shall be made on merit through the procedure notified by the State Government, the affiliating university, or the institution, as applicable, including any reservation policy in force. 2.2 A candidate must have passed the qualifying examination (Higher Secondary / 10+2 or equivalent) with the minimum subjects and marks prescribed for the chosen programme. 2.3 Lateral entry candidates (Diploma holders or B.Sc. graduates, where permitted) shall be admitted directly to the third semester, subject to bridge courses specified by the Board of Studies. 2.4 Admission is provisional until original certificates are verified. Any admission found to be based on false or forged documents shall be cancelled at any stage. 2.5 Transfer of students from other institutions is permitted only where seats are vacant, equivalence of courses is established, and the Academic Council has given approval. 3. PROGRAMME STRUCTURE AND CREDITS 3.1 Each programme is organised into semesters, with the following normal and maximum durations: Programme Semesters Normal Duration Maximum Duration 4-year Bachelor's (B.E. / B.Tech.) 8 4 years 7 years 3-year Bachelor's (B.Sc. / B.Com. / BBA) 6 3 years 5 years Lateral Entry (B.E. / B.Tech.) 6 3 years 6 years 3.2 The curriculum comprises the following course categories: Basic Sciences, Humanities and Management, Core Courses, Professional Electives, Open Electives, Laboratory Courses, Mini Project / Project Work, Internships, and Mandatory Non-credit Courses.

[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 4 3.3 A student shall earn the minimum total credits prescribed in the approved curriculum (for example, 160 credits for a 4-year B.E. / B.Tech. programme) to be eligible for the degree. 3.4 A student may register for a minimum of 16 and a maximum of 28 credits in a semester, unless otherwise permitted by the Academic Council. 3.5 Internships, value-added courses, and online courses (such as NPTEL / SWAYAM) may be credited as per the credit-transfer guidelines approved by the Academic Council. 4. ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENTS 4.1 A student shall be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination only if the student has put in a minimum of 75% attendance in aggregate of all courses in the semester. 4.2 Condonation of shortage of attendance up to 10% (i.e. between 65% and 75%) may be granted by the Principal on medical or other genuine grounds, supported by documents and on payment of the prescribed condonation fee. 4.3 Students with attendance below 65% shall not be permitted to appear for the end-semester examination and shall repeat the semester with the subsequent batch. 4.4 Up to 10 days of attendance may be granted for representing the institution or the university in sports, cultural, or technical events, on the recommendation of the HoD and with prior approval. 4.5 Attendance shall be computed from the date of commencement of classes, and consolidated attendance shall be displayed to students at least twice per semester. 5. REGISTRATION AND COURSE ENROLMENT 5.1 Every student must register for the courses of the semester within the dates notified in the academic calendar, after clearing all dues. 5.2 Registration for electives shall be done in consultation with the faculty advisor. Elective courses are offered only if a minimum number of students (normally 15) enrol. 5.3 Add / drop of courses is permitted within the first two weeks of the semester, subject to the minimum and maximum credit limits. 5.4 Each student shall be assigned a faculty advisor who guides the student on course selection, academic progress and well-being. 6. ASSESSMENT AND EXAMINATIONS 6.1 Performance in each course is assessed through Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) and the End-Semester Examination (ESE), with the weightage below: Course Type Internal (CIA) End-Semester (ESE) Minimum to Pass Theory 40 marks 60 marks 40% in ESE and 50% overall Laboratory 60 marks 40 marks 50% overall Project / Viva 50 marks 50 marks 50% overall

[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 5 6.2 Continuous internal assessment for theory courses shall include at least two periodic tests (best of the two considered), assignments, quizzes, and other activities as specified by the course instructor. 6.3 End-semester examinations shall ordinarily be of three hours' duration for theory courses and shall cover the entire syllabus. 6.4 A student who is absent for an internal test for a valid reason may be allowed a make-up test, with the approval of the HoD. 6.5 The Controller of Examinations shall be responsible for the conduct of examinations, valuation, publication of results, and maintenance of confidential records. 6.6 Examination hall rules: students must carry their identity card and hall ticket, and shall not carry mobile phones, smart watches, or any unauthorised material into the examination hall. 7. GRADING SYSTEM AND CGPA 7.1 Marks obtained in each course shall be converted into letter grades on a 10-point scale as follows: Marks (%) Letter Grade Grade Point Remarks 90 - 100 O 10 Outstanding 80 - 89 A+ 9 Excellent 70 - 79 A 8 Very Good 60 - 69 B+ 7 Good 55 - 59 B 6 Above Average 50 - 54 C 5 Pass Below 50 RA 0 Reappear - AB 0 Absent 7.2 SGPA = Σ(Ci × Gi) / ΣCi, where Ci is the credit of course i and Gi is the grade point obtained in that course, summed over all courses registered in the semester. 7.3 CGPA is computed in the same manner, over all courses registered in all completed semesters, excluding non-credit courses. 7.4 Where a course has been repeated, the grade obtained in the latest attempt shall be used for computing CGPA, and the earlier attempt shall be shown in the record of performance. 7.5 An approximate percentage may be reported as: Percentage = CGPA × 10, if required for external purposes. 8. PROMOTION AND PROGRESSION 8.1 A student shall be promoted from one semester to the next if the student satisfies the attendance requirement and has registered for the semester examinations. 8.2 Promotion from the second year to the third year (and similarly from the third to the fourth year) shall require that the student has cleared all courses of the first two semesters (respectively the first four semesters), subject to a maximum of [two] pending courses, as specified by the Academic

[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 6 Council. 8.3 A student who fails to satisfy the conditions in 8.2 shall be detained until the conditions are met in a subsequent supplementary or regular examination. 8.4 The total period for completing the programme must not exceed the maximum duration specified in Section 3. 9. RE-EVALUATION, SUPPLEMENTARY AND ARREAR EXAMINATIONS 9.1 A student who obtains RA or AB in a course shall reappear for the examination in that course in the immediately following examination session(s). 9.2 A student may apply for photocopy of the answer script and for re-evaluation, within seven days of publication of results, on payment of the prescribed fee. 9.3 Where re-evaluation results in a change of marks, the revised marks shall be taken as final. Where the difference exceeds the limit prescribed by the Controller of Examinations, a third evaluation shall be done. 9.4 Supplementary examinations may be conducted for final-year students having a limited number of pending courses, as notified by the CoE. 9.5 A student may apply for improvement of grade in not more than [two] theory courses, if the student wishes to improve a pass grade, within one year of completing the programme. 10. ACADEMIC INTEGRITY AND MALPRACTICE 10.1 Plagiarism, copying, impersonation, fabrication of data, or possession of unauthorised materials during an examination shall constitute academic misconduct. 10.2 Cases of malpractice shall be referred to the Malpractice Enquiry Committee, which shall give the student an opportunity to be heard. Penalties, depending on gravity, may range from cancellation of the paper concerned to cancellation of all papers of the semester, and, in serious cases, debarment for one or more semesters or dismissal. 10.3 Submission of project reports and assignments shall be accompanied by an undertaking of originality. Similarity beyond the limit prescribed by the institution (normally 15%, excluding references) shall require revision. 10.4 Use of generative AI tools in assignments and projects is permitted only as specified by the course instructor, and any such use must be disclosed. 11. DISCIPLINE AND CODE OF CONDUCT 11.1 Students shall maintain decorum on and off the campus, shall wear the prescribed identity card within the campus, and shall comply with the dress code notified by the institution. 11.2 Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited and is a punishable offence under law. The institution maintains an Anti-Ragging Committee and Squad as per UGC / AICTE regulations. 11.3 Harassment of any kind, including sexual harassment, is prohibited. Complaints shall be handled by the Internal Complaints Committee in accordance with applicable law.

[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 7 11.4 Possession or consumption of alcohol, tobacco, narcotic drugs or other prohibited substances on campus is prohibited. Damage to institutional property shall be recovered from the persons responsible. 11.5 Violation of this code may attract disciplinary action such as warning, fine, suspension, or expulsion, as decided by the Disciplinary Committee. 12. LEAVE, WITHDRAWAL AND RE-ADMISSION 12.1 Leave of absence shall be applied for in advance, wherever possible, through the faculty advisor and HoD. Medical leave shall be supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner. 12.2 A student may be permitted to take a break of study for up to two semesters on genuine grounds, such as ill-health or entrepreneurship, with approval of the Principal. The break period shall be counted within the maximum duration of the programme. 12.3 A student who wishes to discontinue the programme shall submit a written request along with clearance of all dues. Fee refund shall follow the policy notified by the institution and by the regulatory authorities. 12.4 Re-admission after a break shall be allowed in the same or a revised curriculum, subject to equivalence determined by the HoD. 13. AWARD OF DEGREE, CLASSIFICATION AND HONOURS 13.1 A student shall be eligible for the award of the degree if the student has: (a) successfully completed all courses and earned the minimum credits prescribed; (b) completed all mandatory non-credit requirements, including internship; (c) obtained a CGPA of at least 5.0; and (d) no disciplinary action pending. 13.2 Classification shall be based on CGPA, and on completion of the programme within the normal duration, as follows: Class CGPA Condition First Class with Distinction 8.50 and above Cleared all courses in first attempt within normal duration First Class 6.50 to 8.49 Within the maximum duration Second Class 5.00 to 6.49 Within the maximum duration 13.3 Rank certificates and medals shall be awarded only to students who complete the programme in the normal duration without any history of arrears or disciplinary action. 13.4 Students with a CGPA of 8.0 or above at the end of a given semester may be placed on the Dean's List, as recognition of academic excellence. 14. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL AND INTERPRETATION 14.1 Students may submit grievances relating to academics, evaluation, or administration to the Grievance Redressal Committee, which shall respond within 15 working days.

[Institution Name] - Academic Regulations Page 8 14.2 The Principal may, in exceptional circumstances, relax any provision of these regulations in the interest of a student, with the approval of the Academic Council, provided it does not conflict with statutory requirements. 14.3 Any matter not specifically covered by these regulations shall be decided by the Academic Council, whose decision shall be final. 14.4 The institution reserves the right to amend these regulations from time to time. Amendments shall apply from the date notified and shall be communicated to students. *** End of Regulations ***

Electives are offered only with a minimum enrolment of [15] students. 7. LABORATORIES, PROJECTS AND INTERNSHIPS 7.1 Each laboratory course requires a record of experiments and is evaluated through continuous assessment (60 marks) and an end-semester practical examination (40 marks). 7.2 Mini Project (Semester VI): A team project (up to [4] students) under a faculty guide, with review presentations and a report. 7.3 Internship: A minimum of [4] weeks of industrial training or research internship after Semester IV or VI, with a certificate and report. 7.4 Project Work (Semesters VII-VIII): An individual or team project, evaluated through three reviews, a project report, and a final viva-voce examination before an external examiner.

[Institution Name] - Course and Syllabus Information Page 7 8. A pass (satisfactory completion) is required for the award of the degree. 8.2 Credits may be earned through approved MOOCs (NPTEL / SWAYAM / Coursera), up to a maximum of [12] credits, subject to prior approval of the department and submission of the course certificate. 8.3 Value-added certificate courses are offered during semester breaks in areas such as cloud platforms, data analytics, and soft skills. 9. COURSE OUTCOME ATTAINMENT AND CURRICULUM REVISION 9.1 Attainment of Course Outcomes (COs), Programme Outcomes (POs), and Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs) shall be assessed each semester through direct (examination results) and indirect (survey) methods. 9.2 The curriculum shall be reviewed every [two to three] years by the Board of Studies, which includes academic experts, industry representatives, and alumni. *** End of Document ***

[Institution Name] - Examination Regulations Page 3 1. SCOPE AND EXAMINATION AUTHORITIES 1.1 These regulations govern the conduct of internal and end-semester examinations for all programmes of the institution. 1.2 The Controller of Examinations (CoE) is responsible for scheduling, conduct, valuation, result publication, and confidential records. The Examination Committee, chaired by the Principal, oversees policy and resolves exceptional cases. 1.3 The Chief Superintendent is in overall charge of each examination centre, assisted by Hall Superintendents, invigilators, and the flying squad. 2. TYPES OF EXAMINATIONS 2.1 Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA): periodic tests, assignments, quizzes, and laboratory records conducted by the course instructor. 2.2 End-Semester Examination (ESE): a written examination covering the whole syllabus, conducted centrally by the CoE. 2.3 Practical / Viva-voce Examinations: conducted by one internal and one external examiner appointed by the CoE. 2.4 Supplementary / Arrear Examinations: conducted for students who have failed or been absent in earlier attempts. 2.5 Project Evaluation: reviews held during the semester followed by a final viva-voce before a committee including an external expert. 3. ELIGIBILITY AND REGISTRATION FOR EXAMINATIONS 3.1 A student is eligible to appear for the ESE only if he or she satisfies the attendance requirement, has completed the required internal assessments, and has no pending dues or disciplinary action. 3.2 Examination registration must be completed within the dates notified by the CoE, with payment of the prescribed fees. Late registration is permitted only with a late fee until [three] days before the first examination. 3.3 Hall tickets shall be issued only to eligible students and must be produced at every examination along with the college identity card. 3.4 A student whose name does not appear on the registration list shall not be permitted to write the examination under any circumstance. 4. EXAMINATION SCHEDULE AND TIMETABLE 4.1 The tentative examination timetable shall be published at least [three] weeks before the commencement of the examinations; the final timetable shall be published at least [one] week before. 4.2 Each theory examination is of three hours' duration unless otherwise specified. Reporting time is 20 minutes before the start. Candidates shall not be admitted after 30 minutes from the start and shall not leave the hall during the first 60 minutes.

[Institution Name] - Examination Regulations Page 4 4.3 Changes to the timetable are made only by the CoE with the approval of the Principal, and shall be communicated through the official notice board and website. 5. INTERNAL ASSESSMENT PROCEDURE 5.1 Internal marks shall be awarded transparently. Evaluated answer scripts and marks must be shown to students within [seven] working days of the test, with an opportunity to raise queries. 5.2 The distribution of internal marks for a theory course is as follows: Component Marks Remarks Periodic Test 1 and 2 (best / average) 25 Conducted by the department Assignments / Case studies 10 Rubric-based evaluation Attendance 5 Slab-based allocation Total (CIA) 40 Submitted to the CoE before ESE 5.3 Marks for attendance are awarded as: 75-79% = 1; 80-84% = 2; 85-89% = 3; 90-94% = 4; 95% and above = 5. 5.4 Internal marks, once submitted to the CoE, shall not be changed except by the Examination Committee on a written request from the HoD. 6. CONDUCT OF END-SEMESTER EXAMINATIONS 6.1 Candidates must occupy the seat allotted to them. Seating arrangements shall be displayed outside the examination hall 30 minutes before the start. 6.2 Only items permitted by the CoE (pen, pencil, geometry box, approved calculator, and any specific material allowed for the paper) may be brought into the hall. 6.3 Mobile phones, smart watches, earphones, and electronic devices are strictly prohibited and shall be deposited outside the hall. Possession inside the hall is treated as malpractice. 6.4 Answer booklets shall be issued with a unique serial number. Candidates must write the register number only in the space provided, and shall not write their name or leave any identifying mark on the answer sheets. 6.5 Additional answer sheets shall be issued only by the invigilator, and must be tagged to the main booklet. 6.6 Candidates who feel unwell during the examination shall inform the invigilator, who will arrange medical assistance. Extra time shall not ordinarily be granted. 6.7 Differently-abled candidates may avail themselves of a scribe, extra time (up to [20] minutes per hour), and other facilities as approved by the CoE on prior request supported by a valid certificate. 7. MALPRACTICE AND DISCIPLINARY ACTION 7.1 The following acts, among others, constitute malpractice: copying from another candidate; possessing notes or electronic devices; impersonation; tampering with answer sheets; communicating with others in the hall; and misbehaviour toward examination staff.

[Institution Name] - Examination Regulations Page 5 7.2 The invigilator shall seize the evidence, record a statement of the candidate, and report to the Chief Superintendent immediately, allowing the candidate to complete the paper. 7.3 The Malpractice Enquiry Committee shall give the candidate an opportunity to explain and shall recommend penalties as follows: Nature of Offence Normal Penalty Possession of unauthorised material, not used Cancellation of that paper Copying / use of unauthorised material Cancellation of all papers of that session Impersonation / tampering with answer sheets Cancellation of all papers; debarment for one to four semesters Violence or threat to staff; repeated offences Expulsion from the institution 7.4 The decision of the Examination Committee shall be communicated in writing, and the student may appeal to the Principal within [seven] days. 8. VALUATION AND MODERATION 8.1 Answer scripts shall be coded (dummy numbers) and valued by faculty appointed by the CoE, following a scheme of valuation approved by the Board of Examiners. 8.2 Where the difference between two valuations exceeds [15] per cent of the maximum marks, a third valuation shall be conducted and the average of the nearest two marks shall be taken. 8.3 Moderation of marks, where required to ensure uniform standards, shall be done by the Result Passing Board and recorded in its minutes. 8.4 All persons involved in valuation shall maintain strict confidentiality and shall not communicate marks to students before the official publication of results. 9. RESULTS, RE-TOTALLING AND RE-EVALUATION 9.1 Results shall ordinarily be published within [30] days of the last examination, through the student portal and the notice board. 9.2 A student may apply for a photocopy of the evaluated answer script within [seven] days of publication, and, after viewing it, for re-evaluation within [three] days, on payment of the prescribed fee. 9.3 Revaluation applies to theory courses only. The revised mark shall be the final mark, whether higher or lower, except where the difference is within the permitted tolerance. 9.4 Errors in totalling or transfer of marks, when detected, shall be corrected without a fee. 9.5 A provisional mark statement is issued after each semester. Consolidated mark statements, a provisional certificate, and the degree certificate shall be issued after completion of the programme, subject to clearance of dues.

[Institution Name] - Examination Regulations Page 6 10. SUPPLEMENTARY EXAMINATIONS AND ARREARS 10.1 A student who obtains RA (reappear) or AB (absent) shall appear for the failed course in the next available examination session. 10.2 The maximum number of attempts for a course is [six]. Students who exhaust the permitted attempts shall be discharged from the programme, unless the Academic Council permits otherwise. 10.3 The internal marks earned in the course shall be retained for subsequent attempts; a student may choose to re-do the internals by re-registering for the course. 11. SPECIAL PROVISIONS 11.1 A student who is absent in the ESE on account of serious illness, bereavement, or similar grounds may apply for a special examination within [seven] days, supported by documents, which may be granted by the Principal on the CoE's recommendation. 11.2 In the event of public emergencies, natural calamities, or other unforeseen situations, the CoE may reschedule or modify the mode of examinations as approved by the Principal and Academic Council. 11.3 Any matter not covered by these regulations shall be decided by the Examination Committee. Its decision shall be final. *** End of Document ***

[Institution Name] - Fee Structure Page 3 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS 1.1 This document sets out the fees payable by students for the academic year [2026-27]. All amounts are in Indian Rupees (INR) and are illustrative; the institution shall fill in the actual amounts approved by the competent authority. 1.2 Fees for approved (regulated) seats shall conform to the fee fixed by the State Fee Regulatory Committee or the equivalent body. Fees shall not be charged in excess of the fixed amount, and no capitation fee shall be demanded or collected. 1.3 Fees are payable per academic year, in the instalments described in Section 5, through the online payment portal, demand draft, or at the designated bank counter. 2.
